CITY OF ALHAMBRA
  AGENDA
  ALHAMBRA PLANNING COMMISSION
  FEBRUARY 16, 2021
  CORONAVIRUS (COVID-19) ADVISORY NOTICE
Consistent with Executive Orders No. N-29-20 and No. N-35-20 from the Executive Department of the
State of California and the County of Los Angeles Department of Public Health Safer At Home Order, the
Alhambra Planning Commission meeting will not be physically open to the public and the meeting will
take place via teleconference and video conference.

To watch and listen to the meeting: To maximize public safety while still maintaining transparency and
public access, members of the public can participate by using Zoom Webinar as follows:

Zoom Webinar direct link:
https://us02web.zoom.us/j/82735405361
Webinar ID: 827 3540 5361

Or by telephone by dialing 1-888-475-4499 (Toll Free) or 1-833-548-0276 (Toll Free) or 1-833-548-0282
(Toll Free) or 1-877-853-5257 (Toll Free) or 1-669-900-9128 or 1-346-248-7799 or 1-253-215-8782 or 1-
646-558-8656 or 1-301-715-8592 or 1-312-626-6799 and entering Webinar ID: 827 3540 5361. Please
Note: All members of the public calling or logging into the meeting will be muted so that the meeting can
proceed.

For those wishing to speak on an agenda item, please email Principal Planner Paul Lam at
plam@cityofalhambra.org no later than 4:30 p.m. prior to the meeting with the item number you wish to
speak on and the phone number you will use when calling or the name you will use when logging into
the meeting. You should then call or log into the meeting at least 10 minutes prior to its start time. Staff
will unmute you and announce you when it is your time to speak. You will have five minutes to speak,
unless that time is adjusted by the President. If you do not have access to a computer please call 626-570-
5034 to request public comment.

As an alternative to speaking during the meeting, you can email your comments to the Planning Division
at plam@cityofalhambra.org no later than 4:30 p.m. on February 16, 2021 to ensure that Planning Staff
has time to print the emails prior to the beginning of the meeting. Comments will then be read into the
record, with a maximum allowance of 5 minutes per individual comment, subject to the President’s
discretion. If a comment is received after 4:30 p.m. but before the conclusion of the meeting based upon
its time stamp, the comment will still be included as a part of the record of the meeting but will not be
read into the record.

Any member of the public who needs accommodations or who needs their comments translated should
email or call the Community Development Department at plam@cityofalhambra.org or (626) 570-5034.
All requests for accommodations or translation services shall be made by 4 p.m. the Thursday prior to the
Planning Commission meeting. If accommodation or translation is not requested by 4 p.m. the Thursday
prior to the Planning Commission meeting, staff will try to accommodate the request to the best of their
efforts to provide as much accessibility as possible while also maintaining public safety. Given the
challenges of teleconference and video conference meetings, all participants are encouraged to email
their comments prior to the beginning of the meeting.

 AGENDA ITEMS: Copies of the staff reports or other written documentation relating to each item of
 business described herein above are on file in the offices of the Community Development Department in
 City Hall, 111 South First Street, Alhambra, California, and are available on the City’s website. If you
 would like to sign-up to receive the Planning Commission meeting agenda and staff reports packet,

 APPEALS: Any person wishing to appeal any decision of the Planning Commission to the City Council
 may do so by filing an appeal in writing along with the appropriate appeal fee to the Community
 Development Department in City Hall within 10 calendar days of the Planning Commission decision. The
 appeal period for items on this agenda expires at the close of business on March 1, 2021.

  Meeting Rules and Regulations

Section 2.24.060 of the Alhambra Municipal Code provides for the Planning Commission to establish and enforce
its own rules and regulations for its meetings. The Planning Commission uses those rules and regulations
established by the Municipal Code and implemented for use by the City Council.

Addressing the Commission: Any person wishing to address the Commission during the meeting must email Paul
Lam at plam@cityofalhambra.org no later than 4:30 p.m. prior to the meeting with the item number you wish
to speak on and the phone number you will use when calling or the name you will use when logging into the
meeting. You should then call or log into the meeting at least 10 minutes prior to its start time.

As an alternative you can email your comments by sending them to the Planning Division by email at
plam@cityofalhambra.org no later than 4:30 p.m. to ensure that Planning Staff has time to print the emails prior
to the beginning of the meeting. Comments will then be read into the record, with a maximum allowance of 5
minutes per individual comment, subject to the President’s discretion.

All remarks shall be addressed to the Commission as a body and not to any member thereof. No person, other
than the Commission and the person having the floor, shall be permitted to enter into any discussion, either
directly or through a member of the Commission, without the permission of the President. No question shall be
asked a Commissioner except through the President.

Standards of Decorum: Any person addressing the Commission who refuses to stop speaking after his/her time
has expired or any person who behaves in such a manner as to interfere with or impede the progress of the
Planning Commission meeting who, after a request by the President, refuses to cease such behavior may be
muted upon direction of the President.

FROM  Marc Castagnola, AICP, Director of Community DevelopmentMC

SUBJECT:  Planned Development Permit PD-20-24 and Variance VAR-20-06

  1.  LOCATION:  30 W Main Street

  2.  DATE FILED:  August 5, 2020

  3.  APPLICANT:  Peter Pun

  4.  PROPERTY OWNER:  Mu Yang Family LLC

  5.  APN:  5344-033-017

  6.  AREA OF PROPERTY:  3,575 sf. (0.08 acres approximately)

  7.  ZONING:  CBD-DRD (Central Business District-
  Downtown Revitalization District)

  8.  GENERAL PLAN:  Central Business District, Downtown
  Specific Plan Overlay

  9.  CEQA DETERMINATION:  Categorically Exempt

  10.  STAFF RECOMMENDATION:  Approval

PROPOSAL
This is an application for a Commercial Planned Development Permit and Variance to establish a
tea shop in an existing commercial lease space located in the CBD (Central Business District-
Downtown Revitalization District) zone.

LOCATION
The site is located on the south side of Main Street, mid-block, between South Garfield Avenue
and South First Street. The site is also located in the Downtown Revitalization District and is
surrounded by commercial and mixed-use buildings with a variety of uses including restaurants,
retail stores, professional offices, and technical and professional schools. The property measures

  PD 20-24 & VAR 20-06
  Page 1 of 22
 3,575 square feet in size and is improved with a one-story, 3,030 square foot, single-tenant
building. In addition to the frontage along Main Street, the subject property and building is also
accessible from an alley located at the rear.

ANALYSIS
The Applicant is requesting approval of a Planned Development Permit and a Variance to allow
the conversion of the building from retail into a tea shop. The interior will be remodeled to create
a 3,030 square foot space consisting of the dining area, kitchen/service area, and two (2) restrooms.
Within the existing unit there is 912 square foot area at the back consisting of two (2) offices, a
storage room, and a hallway leading to the rear alley. The dining area is proposed to have 13 tables
with seating for 36 people. The business will be operated as a tea shop offering a selection of
different teas. The business will be open from 12:00 P.M. to 10 P.M. Monday through Sunday.

Planned Development Permit
A Planned Development Permit is required for any application of occupancy for the use of a
building which has been vacant for more than six months under the Alhambra Municipal Code
Section 23.62.020(B). The previous occupant of the property at 30 W Main Street was a retail
shop. The last day of occupancy for the retail shop was October 18, 2018, since then the building
has remained vacant for a total of 27 months. Given the extent of time that the building has been
vacant a Planned Development Permit is required per the AMC.

Parking Variance
The subject site is built out with a single story commercial building that has frontage along West
Main Street and alley access at the rear. The site is generally 25 feet wide with 143 feet in depth
and a lot size of approximately 3,575 square feet (0.08 acres). No additions are being proposed as
part of this project. Due to the small size of the property, the Applicant cannot provide parking,
and a Parking Variance will allow the reduction of parking by utilizing the City public parking
lots.

The Alhambra Municipal Code’s parking requirements are based on uses and their floor areas. As
presented in the parking table below, under the AMC §23.52: [Off-Street Parking and Loading
Standards], a food service establishment comprised of 3,030 square feet shall provide a minimum
of 26 parking spaces at a 1:120 ratio, while the previous retail use required a minimum of 13
parking spaces. The proposed business will need 13 more spaces than the previous retail use. As
previously mentioned, the site is already built out and at the time of the building’s construction in
1917 the City did not have on-site parking requirements for businesses. Therefore, no existing on-
site parking spaces or available land area to accommodate new onsite parking spaces is available.

  PARKING REQUIREMENTS

  USE  REQUIRED PARKING
  Previous  Retail  13 spaces
  Proposed  Beverage Establishment  26 spaces

  PD 20-24 & VAR 20-06
  Page 2 of 22
 Under the Zoning Ordinance (Alhambra Municipal Code Section 23.52.060(F)) businesses may
be able to obtain a Parking Variance if the property is within 400 feet of a City-owned public
parking lot. There are two parking structures and one surface parking lot within 400 feet of the
site. The parking structure is located at 80 South First Street, just south of the site and on the same
block. The structure has 158 4-hour parking spaces, 10 twenty-four minute parking spaces, and
82 permit spaces. The other parking structure is located at 26 North First Street. That parking lot
has 225 4-hour parking spaces, 13 twenty-four minute spaces, and 64 permit spaces. Lastly, a
surface parking lot is located at 46 South Second Street and has 28 2-hour parking spaces, five 24
minute spaces, and 17 permit spaces. These three parking facilities provide a total of 602 parking
spaces. It is not uncommon for cities to provide parking for businesses in a downtown district as
they tend to not have room to accommodate parking due to historical development and
transportation practices prior to the advent of the automobile. As mentioned previously, there are
602 parking spaces available from three nearby parking facilities. Therefore, a Parking Variance
is recommended to negate the deficient minimum parking required for a food service establishment
pursuant to AMC Section 23.52.060(F) [Reduction of Requirements].

ENVIRONMENTAL STATUS
This application is categorically exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act, Section
15301, Existing Facilities, Class 1(a) consisting of the permitting, licensing, and leasing involving
negligible or no expansion of the current or former use. No physical expansion of the existing
commercial building is proposed, and the proposed use of the existing building for a tea room is
substantially similar in intensity as the prior use of the building for retail.

PUBLIC NOTICE
On February 3, 2021, a Notice of Public Hearing was sent to 124 property owners of properties
within a 300-foot radius of the project site. A legal notice advertising the public hearing was placed
in the Pasadena Star News on February 4, 2021. A notice was also posted on the property on
February 4, 2020. No comments have been received from any of the parties notified in the area as
of the date this report was finalized.

CONCLUSION
The proposed use will change the parking standards from a 1:250 ratio (retail use) to a 1:120 ratio
(food service establishment use), increasing the overall number of required parking spaces by 13.
However, a Parking Variance will allow the Applicant to utilize the public parking facilities
pursuant to AMC Section 23.52.060(F) [Reduction of Requirements]. The Applicant’s request to
entitle a food service establishment will make Downtown Main Street a more attractive and
pedestrian oriented corridor.

STAFF RECOMMENDED ACTION
Staff recommends Planning Commission to:
  1. Adopt Resolution No. 21-06, approving Planned Development Permit PD-20-24 and
  Variance VAR-20-06 to establish a tea shop in an existing commercial lease space located
  in the CBD-DRD (Central Business District-Downtown Revitalization District) zone,

  West Main Street in the City of Alhambra.

  2. Direct staff to file and post a Notice of Exemption in accordance with Section 15062 of the

THE PLANNING COMMISSION OF THE CITY OF ALHAMBRA DOES HEREBY
RESOLVE AS FOLLOWS:

SECTION 1. FINDINGS OF FACT. The Planning Commission does hereby make the following findings
of fact:

A.  On August 5, 2020, applications for a Planned Development Permit and Variance were submitted by
  the Applicant, Peter Pun, to permit the use of a food service establishment to occupy the existing
  building at 30 West Main Street;

B.  The Planned Development Permit and Variance applications were deemed complete on September
  3, 2020;

C.  The area immediately surrounding the subject site is developed with commercial uses. The subject
  site is located on the south side of Main Street, between South First Street and South Garfield Avenue
  and is currently vacant;

D.  The General Plan land use designation to the north, south, east and west is Central Business District
  and Downtown Revitalization District. The zoning designation to the north, south, east, and west is
  also Central Business District and Downtown Revitalization District;

E.  On February 16, 2021, a duly noticed public hearing was held before the City of Alhambra Planning
  Commission at 7:00 p.m. Consistent with Executive Orders No. N-29-20 and No. N-35-20 from the
  Executive Department of the State of California and the County of Los Angeles Department of Public
  Health Safer At Home Order, the Alhambra Planning Commission meeting was not physically open
  to the public and all Commission Members video conferenced into the meeting; and

F.  At this hearing, the Planning Commission considered the staff report, staff presentation, applicant
  presentation, and public testimony.

SECTION 2. CALIFORNIA ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY ACT FINDINGS. Based upon the
Notice of Exemption prepared for the project, the Planning Commission further finds and determines as
follows:

A.  A Notice of Exemption for this project was prepared in compliance with the California
  Environmental Quality Act (CEQA);

 B.  This project is exempt from the provisions of CEQA per Article 19: Categorical Exemptions,
  Section 15301: Existing Facilities, Class 1(a); interior and exterior alterations to an existing
  structure involving negligible or no expansion of use beyond the existing commercial structure –
  Existing Facilities, Class 1(a);

C.  The documents and other material that constitute the record of proceedings upon which the decision
  of the Planning Commission is based are a Planned Development Permit PD-20-24 and Variance
  VAR-20-06 and that this project file is located within the Community Development Department;
  and

D.  The Planning Commission based upon the findings set forth herein, hereby finds the Notice of
  Exemption for this project has been prepared in compliance with CEQA.

SECTION 3. PLANNED DEVELOPMENT PERMIT FINDINGS. Based upon the foregoing facts and
findings (Section 23.62.070 of the Alhambra Municipal Code) for Planned Development Permit PD 20-24,
the Planning Commission hereby determines as follows:

A.  The proposed use is permitted under the Zoning Ordinance.

  This application for a Planned Development Permit is required pursuant to Section 23.62.020(B)(4)
  since the proposed food service establishment use contains a more restrictive parking standard than
  the previous retail use. However, entitling the proposed food service establishment use is permitted
  in the CBD (Central Business District) zone.

B.  With appropriate conditioning, the proposed use complies with the purpose and intent of the Zoning
  Ordinance and the City’s General Plan.

  The purpose and intent of the Zoning Ordinance and General Plan are to allow for the establishment
  of a mixture of commercial uses. The proposed tea shop is considered a restaurant use and is
  permitted in the Central Business District. The proposed Planned Development Permit is required
  to allow a restaurant use that has a more restrictive parking standard than the previous use. However,
  the property does not provide the required on-site parking required for the proposed use. For the use
  to be permitted under the Zoning Ordinance, the Applicant has requested a Variance to satisfy the
  parking requirement.

C.  With appropriate conditioning, the proposed development would be physically suitable for the lot
  or lots on which it is proposed.

  The subject site is built out with a single story commercial building that has frontage along West
  Main Street and alley access at the rear. The site is generally 25 feet wide with 143 feet in depth and
  a lot size of approximately 3,575 square feet (0.08 acres). No additions are being proposed as part
  of this project. Due to the small size of the property, the Applicant cannot provide parking, and a
  Parking Variance will allow the reduction of parking by utilizing the City public parking lots.

D.  With appropriate conditioning, the proposed development would be physically compatible with
  existing and future land uses within the general area in which the proposed use is located.

  PD 20-24 & VAR 20-06
  Page 12 of 22
   The commercial building is located on a fully built-out portion of West Main Street that consists of
  commercial uses. The proposed tea shop is a restaurant use that will be occupying a commercial
  space that once was a retail shop. There are no additions proposed as part of the scope of work and
  the new restaurant business will be only be utilizing the existing building envelope. Therefore, the
  proposed development would be physically compatible with existing and future land uses within the
  general area.

E.  With appropriate conditioning, there would be adequate provisions for water, sanitation and public
  utilities and services to insure that the proposed use would not be detrimental to public health and
  safety.

  The proposed project has been reviewed by the City of Alhambra Utilities and Public Works
  Departments, who have determined that the subject site and proposed use will be adequately
  serviced with water, sanitation and public utility services to insure that the proposed use would not
  be detrimental to the public health and safety. The proposed use will comply with all applicable
  requirements of the National Pollution Discharge Elimination System permit program and the City
  of Alhambra Low Impact Development Ordinance.

F.  With appropriate conditioning, there would be adequate provisions to public access to serve the
  site.

  Due to the fact that the site is built out and has a narrow width of the lot (25 feet in width), the
  proposed project will not be able to provide the minimum number of parking spaces as required by
  the Zoning Ordinance. The remainder of the parking will be provided within three (3) public parking
  facilities generally to the south, north, and east of the subject site accessible from 1st and 2nd Streets.
  Under the Zoning Ordinance businesses may be able to obtain a Parking Variance if the property is
  within 400 feet of a City-owned public parking lot. The subject property is approximately 100 ft
  away from the First Street Parking facility accessible from South 1st which provides 250 parking
  spaces. The Second Street Parking Lot is located approximately 250 feet away from the subject site
  and would provide 50 parking spaces. The parking structure located at 26 N 1st St is approximately
  270 feet away from the subject site and would provide 302 parking spaces. The collective total of
  parking spaces available within a 400 foot radius of the subject site is 602 parking spaces. Therefore,
  a Parking Variance can be granted to negate the deficient minimum parking required for a food
  restaurant.

SECTION 4. VARIANCE FINDINGS. Based on the forgoing facts and findings (Section 23.68.060 of
the Alhambra Municipal Code) for Variance VAR-20-06, the Planning Commission hereby determines as
follows:

A.  There are special circumstances or exceptional characteristics applicable to the property involved,
  including size, shape, topography, location or surroundings, such that strict application of the
  zoning ordinance deprives such property of privileges enjoyed by other property in the vicinity and
  under the identical zoning classification:

  The subject property was developed in 1917, at which time the City did not require off-street parking
  spaces for commercial uses and the property was developed accordingly, however, off-street parking
  began to be required for commercial uses in 1952. Since the subject property does not comply with
  current off-street parking requirements, the property is legal-nonconforming with respect to parking.

  PD 20-24 & VAR 20-06
  Page 13 of 22
   Pursuant to the Alhambra Municipal Code, food and service establishment uses for the subject
  building’s area would require a total of 26 off-street parking spaces, which the subject property is
  unable to provide since the lot is so narrow (25 feet wide). Alhambra Municipal Code Section
  23.52.060(F) allows the Planning Commission to count City-owned public parking facilities within
  400 feet of a use towards waiving all or part of a development’s on-site parking requirements. There
  are three (3) City-owned public parking facilities within 400 feet of the subject site which will
  provide a total of 602 parking spaces generally to the south, north, and east of the subject site
  accessible from 1st and 2nd Streets. Since a total of 602 public parking spaces are available within a
  400-foot radius of the site, the Planning Commission finds that there will be adequate parking spaces
  to accommodate future food service establishment uses.

B.  The granting of such variance will not be detrimental to the public interest, safety, health or welfare,
  and will not be detrimental or injurious to the property or improvements in the vicinity and zone in
  which the property is located:

  There is a total of 602 public parking spaces provided within a 400-foot radius of the subject site by
  means of parking garages and surface lots located generally to the south, north, and east of the
  subject site accessible from 1st and 2nd Streets. The proposed improvements that will facilitate the
  food service establishment will not increase or expand the area or cause an increased demand in
  parking. There are adequate public parking opportunities within the immediate vicinity that will be
  adequate to accommodate the use. The granting of this Variance will not be detrimental to property
  or improvements in the vicinity and zone since patrons will be able to park in a nearby public parking
  facility and safely access the proposed business.

C.  The granting of such variance will not be contrary to or in conflict with the general purposes and
  intent of the Zoning Ordinance, nor to the goals and programs of the General Plan:

  The granting of the Variance will not be contrary to or in conflict with the general purposes and
  intent of the Zoning Ordinance nor to the goals and programs of the General Plan. The subject site
  currently contains nonconforming on-site parking and is physically unable to provide parking that
  adheres to the Parking Design Standards pursuant to Alhambra Municipal Code (AMC) Section
  23.52.070. The proposed use, would require a total of 26 parking spaces, 13 more than the previous
  retail use, which will be accommodated by the public parking facilities within a 400 foot proximity.
  Utilization of public parking lots to satisfy the parking requirements of a private business is
  authorized by AMC 23.52.060(F), (which allows businesses within 400 feet of a public parking lot
  to count the public spaces toward meeting the business’s parking requirement) and is not contrary
  to or in conflict with the general purposes or intent of the Zoning Ordinance or to the goals and
  programs of the General Plan. The proposed establishment will contribute to the broad range of
  services the Downtown has to offer, which is consistent with the purpose and intent of the Zoning
  Ordinance and the General Plan.

D.  The variance request is consistent with the purpose and intent of the zone in which the site is located:

  The CBD zone is intended to provide for a broad range of retail and service commercial activities
  and uses, operating under development standards designed to create a compatible and harmonious
  setting. The proposed food service establishment use will continue to bring services and menu
  options that will contribute to the broad range of goods and services the Downtown has to offer.
  Developing a diverse quality commercial base supports the purpose and intent of the Zoning
  Ordinance and General Plan.

  PD 20-24 & VAR 20-06
  Page 14 of 22
 SECTION 5. NOW THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, by the Planning Commission of the City of
Alhambra, California, as follows:

A.  Approve Planned Development Permit PD-20-24 and Variance VAR-20-06 to allow a food service
  establishment to occupy the existing building previously used by a retail use located in the CBD-
  DRD (Central Business District-Downtown Revitalization District) zone, subject to the attached
  Conditions of Approval (Exhibit A) for the property located at 30 West Main Street in the City of
  Alhambra.

B.  Direct staff to file and post a Notice of Exemption in accordance with Section 15062 of the California
  Code of Regulations.

SUBJECT:  Status Report Regarding Accessory Dwelling Unit’s (ADU’s)

PURPOSE:

The purpose and intent of the information contained in this status report is to provide the Planning
Commission with a general overview on the number of Accessory Dwelling Unit (“ADU”) applications
submitted to the City, type of ADU’s requested, status of ADU submittals, and location of all ADU’s
within the City.

BACKGROUND:

On September 16, 2019, staff provided the Planning Commission with a report and presentation
regarding the status of Accessory Dwelling Unit’s (ADU’s) throughout the City. A subsequent
presentation was provided to the Planning Commission on May 18, 2020. With additional data now
available, this report builds upon what has been previously presented to the Planning Commission.

In 2016, new State legislation was passed that required local agencies to ministerially consider ADU
applications in all residential zones. The legislation was a result of the statewide housing crisis, rising
housing costs, and a shortage of affordable housing options. The new State law became effective January
1, 2017. The City of Alhambra was required to apply the State’s broader, less restrictive development
regulations outlined in State law, regardless of any impact to the character of an existing neighborhood
unless and until the City adopted its own ordinance. In an effort to meet the City’s unique needs while
still complying with State requirements, the City adopted a new ADU ordinance on December 11, 2017
that became effective on January 27, 2018. A subsequent ordinance amendment followed in July 2018
in an effort to further clarify the requirements with respect to required lot area, width and depth
requirements. The State continues to enact new legislation, including new laws effective as of January
1, 2020.

TYPES OFADU’S

When discussing ADU’s, it is important to understand the type of ADU’s actually being proposed in the
City of Alhambra. ADU applications submitted to the City fall into the following four categories:

  1) New detached structure;
  1
   2) New attached structure (attached to either the existing home or garage that will be
  maintained for parking);
  3) Integration within the existing home (i.e. converting a master bedroom within the primary
  residence into a separate living unit); or
  4) Garage conversion or conversion of other accessory structures.

Table 1 provides a summary of the types of ADU applications submitted to the City for the prior
reporting period presented to the Planning Commission (January 1, 2017 to February 29, 2020) and the
current reporting period covering March 1, 2020 to December 31, 2020. Based on the information
identified in Table 1, a total of 62 applications have been submitted during the current reporting period
and a total of 170 ADU applications have been processed since 2017.
